plan: Diagnose the remaining prose/workflow failures at their shared ownership layers, validate two materially different chapter functions and POVs with real generation/review runs, then refresh the anonymous top-tier prose comparison.
actions: Made endingHook the concrete presentation of the final beat rather than an appended event, and added a blueprint-level single-fulfillment contract across mustHappen, beats, and hook.
Changed revision mustHappen context into a read-only preservation list so local windows cannot inject whole-chapter recaps or advance unrelated requirements.

Hardened shared AI transport handling: retry successful empty completions, flush unterminated final SSE events, retain non-content diagnostics, and use retried non-streaming fallback for prose and structured calls.

Changed deterministic hook evidence from final-paragraph keyword matching to an ending-window pending-choice check, and prevented conditional POV hypotheses without quoted inner-state evidence from becoming majors.
Scoped bench context and chapter fixtures by selected blueprint, then generated and reviewed a different continuation/autopsy chapter under a second POV.
Refreshed anonymous seven-dimension prose comparison against mature Chinese web-fiction technique standards using the two current artifacts.
Ran full unit tests, TypeScript validation, production build, and diff whitespace validation.

errors: Real runs exposed repeated successful-but-empty SSE completions. Diagnostic evidence showed finish=stop and outputTokens=0; the shared transport now retries and falls back across both prose and structured calls.
One review promoted a hypothetical POV interpretation even though its excerpt contained only observable action. Evidence-aware normalization now keeps such conditional claims at warning severity.
selfReflection: The decisive improvement came from treating generated samples and scores as evidence rather than specifications. Duplicate invitations originated in conflicting blueprint/draft contracts, revision corruption originated in a local-window ownership violation, and incomplete reviews originated in shared transport behavior. Fixing those mechanisms produced a clean second scenario without character-name or fixture-specific production rules. The blind comparison still identifies supporting-character voice differentiation and overlapping environmental/process functions as useful future quality work, but they are warnings rather than unmet success criteria.
